comments.author: SeanLuke
comments.story_title: Why Cassettes?
comments.why_zh: 纠正关于数字音频与盒式磁带的迷思。
comments.quote_zh: 这些人应该被绑在椅子上，眼皮被胶带撑开，然后被强行喂看 Monty Montgomery 的视频。
comments.text_zh:
> 发烧友可能会指出，模拟音频源理论上能包含数字音频中听不到的细节。这是对的，因为模拟介质中的值是连续的。在短到无法察觉的时间间隔内，数字录音中代表声波不同值的数字会从一个离散值瞬间跳到另一个离散值，中间没有平缓的斜坡。模拟信号则形成平滑曲线，所以在某种程度上，它们可以包含微小的斜率变化，而这些变化太细微，数字化该信号时无法表示。

> 一般来说，模拟优越性的问题在于，当那个数字信号是标准 CD 音质（每秒 44,100 个采样、16 位分辨率）时，模拟信号中任何细微到无法被数字捕捉的细节，也细微到我和大多数人根本听不见。

这错得让我头疼。都 2023 年了，人们仍然认为数字不会产生平滑曲线，还认为典型的模拟介质——更别提盒式磁带了——能比 CD 存储更多细节。这些人应该被绑在椅子上，眼皮被胶带撑开，然后被强行喂看 Monty Montgomery 的视频。[VIDEO]
comments.text: > Audiophiles might point out that analog audio sources can theoretically hold details you can't hear in digital. This is true because values in analog media are continuous. Over imperceptibly short periods of time, the numbers that represent different values on a sound wave in a digital recording jump instantaneously from one discrete value to another with no gentle slope between. Analog signals instead form smooth curves, so at some level they can contain tiny variations in slope that are too subtle for the digitization of that signal to represent. > The problem with analog superiority in general is that, when that digital signal is of standard CD quality (44,100 samples per second at 16-bit resolution), whatever details in the analog signal are too subtle to be captured digitally are also too subtle for me or really most people to hear. This so wrong it makes my head hurt. It's 2023 and people still think that digital doesn't produce smooth curves and that typical analog media -- cassette tape no less -- can store more details than a CD. These people need to be tied to a chair, have their eyelids taped open, and force-fed Monty Montgomery's video. [VIDEO]

comments.quote_zh: 我参考资料 [1] 里的那个视频值得一看——那是从真正的黑客视角讲数字音频
comments.text_zh: 我参考资料 [1] 里的那个视频值得一看——那是从真正的黑客视角讲数字音频，以及它如何转换到模拟域。即便是 20kHz 的声音，在 44kHz 采样率下也不会有任何混叠。大多数人的听力在 12kHz 左右之后就开始明显衰减（取决于年龄）。据我的经验，大多数镲片的基频在 2-5kHz 左右。而且，因为镲片的声音已经非常接近噪声了，它到底有没有影响其实很难说。不过如果你听 128 kbps 的 MP3，常常能听出高频声音（比如镲片）变得“糊成一团”。对绝大多数人来说，到了 192 kbps 就听不出来了，再往上，就算“金耳朵”的人也很难分辨。而这还是有损格式，更别说我们这里讨论的 CD、WAV 或 FLAC 这些无损格式了。[1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: It's worth watching the video in my references [1] - it's a proper hacker's view of digital audio and how it translates to the analogue domain. Even with a 20khz sound you're not going to get any aliasing at 44khz sample rate. Most people's hearing starts to fall off significantly after around 12khz or so (depending on age). Most cymbals have a fundamental frequency around 2-5khz in my experience. Also, because cymbal sounds are pretty close to being noise, it's arguable whether it would matter or not. Although if you listen to a 128 kbps MP3 then you can often hear the top end frequency sounds (like cymbals) becoming 'mushy'. To the vast majority of people once you get to 192 kbps it's inaudible, and then above that most people with 'perfect ears' would struggle. And that's with a lossy format, never mind the lossless formats of CDs, WAV or FLAC which is the discussion at hand. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.story_title: FLAC 1.4.0 released – added support for 32-bit audio
comments.quote_zh: xipf.org 的 Monty Montgomery 有一个不错的 YouTube 视频与此相关
comments.text_zh: Nyquist-Shannon 简单来说就是：要完美重建某样东西，采样率必须是最高频率的 2 倍。所以，要重建一个以 16 位采样的 20 kHz 波形，就需要 40 kHz 的采样率。把它提高到 22.05 kHz（为了抗混叠），就得到 CD 音频。另一方面，位深是对该音频进行采样/量化时的信噪比（噪声底）。它与 Nyquist-Shannon 无关。位数越多，重建时的噪声越小。对于 CD 音频，选择 16 位是为了给出可接受的 96 dB SNR。xipf.org 的 Monty Montgomery 有一个不错的 YouTube 视频与此相关：[VIDEO]
comments.text: Nyquist-Shannon simply says that you need 2x the sample rate of the highest frequency to perfectly recreate something. So, to recreate a 20 kHz wave that was sampled at 16 bits, you'd need 40 kHz sample rate. Bump that up to 22.05 kHz (for anti-aliasing) and you get CD audio. The bit depth, OTOH, is your signal-noise ratio (noise floor) when sampling/quantizing said audio. It's unrelated to Nyquist-Shannon. More bits gives you less noise when reproducing it. For CD audio, 16 bits was chosen to give an acceptable SNR of 96 dB. Monty Montgomery (of xipf.org) has a nice YouTube video related to this: [VIDEO]

comments.author: ZoomZoomZoom
comments.story_title: Is there anyone here making music?
comments.text_zh: 在声音方面，没有什么比得上亲身经验、实验和数小时的刻意聆听。花几个小时玩玩 DAW 自带的基础压缩器，试着感受并理解每个参数如何影响不同的声音（从正弦波和噪声到人声再到鼓等等）。如果你觉得没收获，就去读、看视频、听、做自己的东西，过一阵再回来。关于书，选择很多。想要一些快速实用的智慧，推荐 Bobby Owsinski 的 Mixing, Recording and Mastering Handbooks（三本分开的）。Mixerman 的 Zen & The Art Of Mixing 非常好，还有他的经典 The Daily Adventures。如果你对录音感兴趣，The Bruce Swedien Recording Method 很不错。至于 YouTube 视频，有些零散的东西我可以保证：我建议看 Monty 的 Digital Show and Tell [1]，作为数字音频这种形式的入门。Steve Albini 最近发布了一些非常扎实又有趣的录音视频 [2]。当然还有几个被热捧（但名副其实）的频道，比如 @DanWorrall、@Producelikeapro 或 @ProductionAdvice。课程我没什么可推荐的，因为我已经有一阵子不感兴趣了。 [1] [VIDEO] [2] [LINK]
comments.text: In sound, nothing beats personal experience, experimentation and hours of deliberate listening. Spend a couple of hours with a basic compressor built-in your DAW and try to get the feel and understanding of how each parameter affects different sounds (from sine wave and noise to voice to drums, etc.). If you feel it's not fruitful, read, watch videos, listen, work on your stuff and come back to it after a while. Regarding books, there's lots to choose from. For some quick applied wisdom, Bobby Owsinski's Mixing, Recording and Mastering Handbooks (separate) are recommended. Zen & The Art Of Mixing by Mixerman is very good, as well as his classic The Daily Adventures. The Bruce Swedien Recording Method is very good if you're into recording. For Youtube videos, some random things I can vouch for: I'd suggest watching Monty's Digital Show and Tell [1] as a primer for digital audio as a form. Steve Albini has been putting out some very solid and entertaining videos on recording lately [2]. There's also of course a few hyped (but deservedly so) channels such as @DanWorrall, @Producelikeapro or @ProductionAdvice. Nothing I can suggest for courses as I haven't been interested in them for a while. [1] [VIDEO] [2] [LINK]

comments.author: spider-mario
comments.story_title: 24-bit/192kHz music downloads and why they make no sense
comments.why_zh: 演示抖动后频谱是平坦的。
comments.quote_zh: 频谱实际上是平坦的，正如你可能暗指的那个视频所展示的
comments.text_zh:
> 出于硬性、客观的原因，16 bit 不够用。原因之一是量化的噪声频谱并不简单。大多数人以为它接近纯白噪声，但事实并非如此。它实际上是一个非常复杂的频谱，在采样率的某些特定分频处有明显的尖峰。

你描述的是粗暴截断的结果。如果你使用最基础的（“均匀”或“矩形”，也叫“RPDF”）抖动，频谱实际上是平坦的，正如你可能暗指、并称之为“伪科学”的那个视频所展示的（[VIDEO]）。如果你把两个均匀抖动叠加在一起，就得到了几乎所有人都在用的东西（“三角”或“TPDF”抖动），它不仅让平均量化误差与信号去相关，也让标准差去相关，从而消除了噪声调制，只在高阶矩（如偏度和峰度）中留下相关性。你甚至可以用 SoX 自己试一下。找一首 24-bit 的音轨，用抖动量化到 16-bit，计算两条音轨之间的差值，放大这个差值并生成它的频谱图，它会完全是平坦的。或者直接听这个差值（注意音量），看看你能不能听出任何有意义的东西。

$ sox source.flac -b 16 dithered.flac
$ sox --combine merge source.flac dithered.flac loud-difference.flac remix 1,3i 2,4i norm -1 spectrogram # assumes stereo input
$ open spectrogram.png
$ open loud-difference.flac

然后再记住，这个差值
comments.text: > 16 bit isn't enough for hard, objective reasons. One is that the noise spectrum of quantisation is not simple. Most people assume it's something close to plain white noise, but it really isn't. It's actually a very complex spectrum with some prominent peaks at specific subdivisions of the sample rate. What you are describing is the result of blunt truncation. If you use the most basic (“uniform” or “rectangular” a.k.a. “RPDF”) dither, the spectrum is in fact flat, as demonstrated by the video you are likely alluding to and calling “pseudoscientific” ( [VIDEO] ). If you sum two uniform dithers together, you get what pretty much everyone uses (“triangular” or “TPDF” dither) which, in addition to decorrelating the mean quantisation error from the signal, also decorrelates the standard deviation, eliminating noise modulation and leaving a correlation only in still higher-order moments like skewness and kurtosis. You can even try it for yourself with SoX. Find a 24-bit track, quantise it with dither to 16-bit, calculate the difference between both tracks, blow up the difference and take its spectrogram and it will be completely flat. Or listen to the difference (mind the volume) and see if you can make out anything meaningful. $ sox source.flac -b 16 dithered.flac $ sox --combine merge source.flac dithered.flac loud-difference.flac remix 1,3i 2,4i norm -1 spectrogram # assumes stereo input $ open spectrogram.png $ open loud-difference.flac And then remember that this difference
